title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), billed as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, and about 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 on average. It is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting, and Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices were halved, which Anthropic says makes most agentic work about 20% cheaper, with Max and Team getting monthly API credit. It targets high-volume work such as classification, summaries, subagents, and live support, while Sonnet and Opus remain better for complex coding.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: Lance Martin and CJ Avilla published a guide to scheduled agents on Claude Managed Agents (beta), using a "daily-brief" reference implementation that pulls from Slack and GitHub PRs and posts a Slack brief. Setup uses config files for the agent, schedule, memory, vault, and network allowlist applied with `ant apply`, running on Anthropic infrastructure, with credentials kept in a vault outside the sandbox, read-only access, and a per-run spending cap. The patterns, including per-source bookmarks, reporting unreadable sources, and confirming posts before updating the ledger, matter because background agents otherwise fail silently.

title: How Comcast and Booz Allen use Claude Mythos to find exploit chains and secure their codebases
summary: Security teams used Claude Mythos-class models through the limited-access Project Glasswing to find and fix vulnerabilities. Comcast found a critical authentication flaw across 258 systems and about 170M lines of code and fixed it before exploitation, while Booz Allen traced a boot-time key-protection flaw across two programs and languages, with one analyst covering 8 systems and 138 repos in 12 days. The models connect code, config, identity, and deployment context to surface cross-component exploit chains, and validating findings is now the bottleneck.

title: Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI
summary: In an interview, Uber CISO Philip Martin describes treating AI agents as insider-threat subjects. Uber's open-source AI Detection and Response (ADR) tool works with Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which let Uber keep data control and choose responses, with classifier output feeding ADR as a real-time signal. Newer models pull context from code, design docs, and Jira for more specific threat modeling, and Uber's priorities are real-time detection near prompt entry and ongoing analysis of new model behaviors.

title: We're expanding the Claude Startups program to help founders build
summary: Anthropic expanded the Claude Startups program to admit more founders, offering up to $7,000 in products and credits, including a free year of Claude Team with up to 5 Premium seats and a one-time $1,000 API credit. A new Claude Startup Stack adds discounts and credits worth up to $45,000 on company tools, alongside office hours with the Applied AI team, Claude Marketplace listing help, events, and a newsletter. As of an Oct 13 update, the current cohort is full and applications are closed for now.

title: Automating eval design and hillclimbing with Claude
summary: Anthropic published guidance on designing evals and hillclimbing without overfitting, shipped as two claude-api skill commands. `/claude-api build-eval` interviews you, samples production-like inputs, proposes the cheapest suitable grader, and runs diagnostics, while `/claude-api hillclimb` splits train and test sets and keeps each proposed patch only if both sets improve. Examples include an ~80% cut in cost per ticket with better held-out accuracy, and a skill run that rose from 66% to about 88%.
